question: Your support agent handles disputed charges in two phases. First it must find out what happened, and findings often change the next step; for example, a charge that the customer calls unknown may turn out to be a replacement order created by an earlier return. Then, before any call to process_refund, it must confirm the same four points for every case: refund amount, policy eligibility, identity verification, and payment method. Which design decisions fit these two phases?

options.text: Decompose the first phase dynamically, so the agent generates new subtasks from what each tool result reveals, such as looking up the original returned order.
options.reason: Finding out what happened is an open-ended investigation. The guide matches this to dynamic adaptive decomposition, which generates subtasks from intermediate findings.

options.text: Combine the four pre-refund points into one pass that checks them all together, because the agent already holds the full case context from the first phase.
options.reason: The guide says prompt chaining breaks a predictable review into focused sequential passes. A single combined pass gives up that focus on each point.

options.text: Run the pre-refund phase as a fixed prompt chain with one focused pass for each of the four points, in the same order for every case.
options.reason: Confirming the same four points for every case is a predictable multi-aspect review. The guide matches this to prompt chaining with sequential focused passes.

options.text: Plan every first-phase subtask from the customer's opening message, then execute that plan without changing it after tool results arrive, so each case runs predictably.
options.reason: The first phase is open-ended, and its findings change the next step. The guide says such tasks need a plan that generates subtasks from what each step discovers.

options.text: Let the adaptive investigation also decide which pre-refund points to check, so the agent skips any point that its findings in the first phase make seem irrelevant to the case.
options.reason: The four points are the same known set for every case, so this is a predictable multi-aspect review. The guide matches that to prompt chaining, which does not skip checks.
